bank.name: Angels, Beliefs & Articles of Faith
bank.subject: Islamic Studies
bank.description: The articles of faith, angels and core Islamic beliefs.

questions.prompt: Belief in the books of Allah includes which revealed scriptures?
questions.explanation: Muslims believe in the Taurat (Musa), Zabur (Daud), Injeel (Isa) and the Quran (Muhammad PBUH).

questions.prompt: Who is the angel responsible for blowing the trumpet (Sur) on the Day of Judgment?
questions.explanation: Israfil (AS) will blow the Sur (trumpet) to signal the Day of Resurrection.

questions.prompt: Which angel is the one who takes souls at death?
questions.explanation: Azra'il is the angel of death who takes the souls of the departed.

questions.prompt: The angels who question the dead in the grave are called?
questions.explanation: Munkar and Nakir are the angels who question the deceased in the grave.

questions.prompt: The angels who record good and bad deeds are called?
questions.explanation: Kiraman Katibin are the noble recording angels (Qaf 50:17-18).

questions.prompt: Which angel is the keeper of Paradise (Jannah)?
questions.explanation: Ridwan is the angel guarding Paradise; Malik guards Hell.

questions.prompt: Which angel is the keeper of Hell (Jahannam)?
questions.explanation: Malik is the keeper of Jahannam (Zukhruf 43:77).

questions.prompt: How many angels carry the Throne of Allah on the Day of Judgment?
questions.explanation: The Quran mentions eight angels bearing the Throne on that Day (69:17).

questions.prompt: What is 'Taqdir' (Qadar)?
options: Belief in divine decree, both good and bad
questions.explanation: Taqdir is the belief that all that happens is by Allah's decree and measure.

questions.prompt: What is 'Akhirah'?
options: The afterlife and the Day of Judgment
questions.explanation: Akhirah refers to the eternal life after death, including resurrection and judgment.

questions.prompt: What are the two names for Paradise and Hell in the Quran?
questions.explanation: Jannah (Paradise) and Jahannam (Hell) are the two eternal abodes.

questions.prompt: What is 'Barzakh'?
options: The intermediate state between death and resurrection
questions.explanation: Barzakh is the grave/interim state until the Day of Resurrection.

questions.prompt: What is the 'Sirat'?
options: The bridge over Hell that all must cross
questions.explanation: As-Sirat is the bridge over Jahannam; the righteous cross it to Jannah.

questions.prompt: What is 'Mizan'?
options: The weighing of deeds on the Day of Judgment
questions.explanation: Al-Mizan is the balance in which deeds will be weighed (21:47).

questions.prompt: The first question asked of the dead in the grave is about?
questions.explanation: The deceased is asked: Who is your Lord? What is your religion? Who is your Prophet?

questions.prompt: Which Surah begins by swearing by the 'Day of Resurrection'?
questions.explanation: Surah Al-Qiyamah opens: 'I swear by the Day of Resurrection.'

questions.prompt: The angel Jibra'il (AS) is also called?
questions.explanation: Jibra'il is called Ruh-ul-Qudus and Ruh-ul-Amin in the Quran.

questions.prompt: What are the 'Hafaza' angels?
questions.explanation: Hafaza are the guardian angels appointed over every person (13:11).

questions.prompt: Which angel is entrusted with delivering revelation to the Prophets?
questions.explanation: Jibra'il (Gabriel) is the angel of revelation who conveyed Allah's message to the Prophets.

questions.prompt: Which angel is entrusted with the distribution of sustenance and rain?
questions.explanation: Mika'il (Michael) is responsible for providing sustenance and controlling rain and provisions.

questions.prompt: Which angel is known as the angel of death who takes the souls of people?
questions.explanation: Azra'il (AS), the Angel of Death, is tasked with taking the souls of every living being.

questions.prompt: Who is the keeper of Hell (Jahannam)?
questions.explanation: Malik (AS) is the chief keeper of Hell mentioned in the Quran (43:77).

questions.prompt: Who is the guardian of Paradise (Jannah)?
questions.explanation: Ridwan (AS) is the keeper of Paradise who welcomes the believers.

questions.prompt: What does 'Kiraman Katibin' mean?
questions.explanation: Kiraman Katibin are the noble angels who record every person's good and bad deeds.

questions.prompt: Which angels carry the Throne (Arsh) of Allah?
questions.explanation: Hamalat-ul-Arsh are the angels who bear the Throne of Allah (40:7).

questions.prompt: Which two angels were sent to Babylon and taught people magic as a trial?
questions.explanation: Harut and Marut are mentioned in Surah Al-Baqarah (2:102) as a trial sent to Babylon.

questions.prompt: What is the first article of faith (Iman) in Islam?
questions.explanation: Tawheed — belief in the Oneness of Allah — is the first and most fundamental article of faith.

questions.prompt: What is 'Qadar' in Islamic belief?
questions.explanation: Qadar is the belief that everything happens by Allah's divine decree and measure.

questions.prompt: What is the period between death and the Day of Judgment called?
questions.explanation: Barzakh is the intermediate state between death and resurrection.

questions.prompt: What is the 'Mizan' on the Day of Judgment?
questions.explanation: Mizan is the scale on which every person's good and bad deeds will be weighed.

questions.prompt: What is the 'Sirat' in Islamic eschatology?
options: The bridge over Hell thinner than a hair
questions.explanation: Sirat is the bridge over Hell that everyone must cross; the righteous cross swiftly, the sinful stumble.

questions.prompt: What is 'Hashr' (the Gathering)?
options: All mankind gathered on the plain of judgment
questions.explanation: Hashr is the Day of Gathering when all creation is assembled for judgment.

questions.prompt: What is 'Taqdir' also known as?
questions.explanation: Taqdir is another term for Qadar — Allah's decree and destiny for all creation.

questions.prompt: Which angel recorded the Quranic revelation as it was revealed?
questions.explanation: Jibra'il (AS) brought the revelation to the Prophet (PBUH), who dictated it to the scribes.

questions.prompt: Which angel is responsible for taking souls at death?
questions.explanation: Azrael is the angel of death who takes souls.

questions.prompt: Who was the angel that visited the Prophet (PBUH) in the cave of Hira?
questions.explanation: Jibreel brought the first revelation in Hira.

questions.prompt: The keeper of Hell is known as:
questions.explanation: Malik is the guardian of Jahannam.

questions.prompt: Angels are created from:
questions.explanation: Angels were created from light according to hadith.

questions.prompt: The angel who delivers sustenance and rain is:
questions.explanation: Mikail is responsible for provisions and rain.

questions.prompt: The number of angels carrying the Throne (Arsh) is:
questions.explanation: The Quran mentions eight angels bearing the Throne.

questions.prompt: Belief in angels is one of the:
questions.explanation: Belief in angels is a core article of Iman.

questions.prompt: The angel who carries revelations to other prophets before Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) was:
questions.explanation: Jibreel conveyed revelation to all prophets.

questions.prompt: The guardian of Paradise is:
questions.explanation: Ridwan is the keeper of Jannah.

questions.prompt: Which angels are mentioned by name in the Quran?
questions.explanation: The Quran names Jibreel and Mikail directly.

questions.prompt: The angels do not enter a house containing:
options: A dog or images (as per hadith)
questions.explanation: Hadith states angels avoid homes with dogs or images.

questions.prompt: In the Quran, angels are described as:
questions.explanation: Angels are obedient, honoured servants of Allah.

questions.prompt: The two angels Harut and Marut are mentioned in which context?
options: The trial in Babylon regarding magic
questions.explanation: Harut and Marut are linked to the test of magic in Babylon.

questions.prompt: Angels can take which forms?
questions.explanation: Angels appeared in human form, e.g., to Maryam and Ibrahim.

questions.prompt: The angel that came to Ibrahim (AS) with news of Ishaq was:
questions.explanation: Angels visited Ibrahim with glad tidings.

questions.prompt: Angels do not eat, drink, or:
questions.explanation: Angels have no physical needs and never disobey.

questions.prompt: Who taught Adam (AS) the names of all things as mentioned in the Quran?
questions.explanation: Allah taught Adam the names, then asked the angels about them.

questions.prompt: The angels who protect a person from harm are called:
questions.explanation: Hafaza are the guarding angels assigned to each person.

questions.prompt: In the Quran, Iblis refused to prostrate to Adam because of:
questions.explanation: Iblis refused out of arrogance, claiming superiority.

questions.prompt: According to Surah Fatir, angels are created with how many wings?
questions.explanation: Surah Fatir (35:1) says Allah made angels with wings — two, three and four.

questions.prompt: How many angels are appointed as keepers of Hell according to the Quran?
questions.explanation: Surah Al-Muddaththir (74:30) states: 'Over it are nineteen.'

questions.prompt: What are the 'Zabaniyah'?
questions.explanation: The Zabaniyah are the stern angels appointed over Hell.

questions.prompt: Who gave Zakariyya (AS) the glad tidings of a son (Yahya)?
questions.explanation: In Surah Maryam and Surah Al-Imran, the angels announced Yahya to Zakariyya (AS).

questions.prompt: Which angel conveyed the news of Isa (AS) to Maryam (AS)?
questions.explanation: Jibra'il (AS) appeared to Maryam in the form of a well-made man to give the news of Isa.

questions.prompt: What is 'Iman-e-Mufassal'?
options: The detailed statement of Islamic belief
questions.explanation: Iman-e-Mufassal spells out belief in Allah, His angels, books, messengers, the Last Day and Qadar in detail.

questions.prompt: What is 'Iman-e-Mujmal'?
options: The concise summary of Islamic belief
questions.explanation: Iman-e-Mujmal is the brief declaration of faith in Allah and His attributes as described.

questions.prompt: How many articles of faith (Iman) are there in Islam?
questions.explanation: The six articles are: Allah, angels, revealed books, messengers, the Last Day and divine decree.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is NOT among the six articles of faith?
options: Belief in the Imamate of the Twelve Imams
Belief in the Day of Judgment
questions.explanation: The six articles cover Allah, angels, books, messengers, the Last Day and Qadar; the Twelve-Imam doctrine is not among them.

questions.prompt: What is 'Aqeedah'?
questions.explanation: Aqeedah is the set of beliefs a Muslim holds about Allah and the faith.

questions.prompt: What does 'Kufr' mean?
questions.explanation: Kufr is rejection of or ingratitude towards Allah's guidance.

questions.prompt: What is 'Nifaq' (hypocrisy)?
questions.explanation: Nifaq is showing faith outwardly while concealing disbelief.

questions.prompt: Who are the 'Munafiqun'?
options: Hypocrites who show faith but conceal disbelief
questions.explanation: The Quran repeatedly warns about the Munafiqun, who declare faith but do not believe in their hearts.

questions.prompt: The two recording angels sit on which sides of a person?
questions.explanation: Tradition holds that two angels record deeds from the right and left shoulders.

questions.prompt: Who are the 'Mu'aqqibat' mentioned in Surah Ar-Ra'd?
options: Guardian angels who follow a person in front and behind
questions.explanation: Surah Ar-Ra'd (13:11) mentions guardian angels protecting a person from the front and behind.

questions.prompt: According to the common Islamic belief, the Sur (trumpet) will be blown how many times?
questions.explanation: The first blow stuns creation and the second raises mankind for judgment.

questions.prompt: What is 'Qiyamah'?
questions.explanation: Qiyamah is the Day of Resurrection when all creation is raised for judgment.

questions.prompt: What is the 'A'raf'?
options: The elevated heights between Paradise and Hell
questions.explanation: Surah Al-A'raf describes the people of the Heights standing between Jannah and Jahannam.

questions.prompt: Which tree is mentioned in the Quran as growing in Hell?
questions.explanation: Zaqqum is the bitter tree of Hell mentioned in several surahs.

questions.prompt: What is 'Salsabil'?
questions.explanation: Salsabil is a spring in Paradise mentioned in Surah Al-Insan (76:18).

questions.prompt: What is 'Kawthar'?
options: A river and pool in Paradise granted to the Prophet (PBUH)
questions.explanation: Surah Al-Kawthar (108) refers to the abundant river granted to the Prophet (PBUH).

questions.prompt: What are 'Sijjin' and 'Illiyyin'?
options: Records of the wicked and of the righteous
questions.explanation: Surah Al-Mutaffifin mentions the register of the wicked (Sijjin) and of the righteous (Illiyyin).

questions.prompt: Who is traditionally regarded as the chief of the angels?
questions.explanation: Jibra'il (AS) is regarded as the leader of the angels, entrusted with revelation.

questions.prompt: By Allah's command, the angels prostrated before whom?
questions.explanation: Allah commanded the angels to prostrate to Adam (AS), and Iblis alone refused.

questions.prompt: Which angels were sent to punish the people of Lut (AS)?
questions.explanation: Angels led by Jibra'il (AS) turned the towns of Lut's people upside down.

questions.prompt: The angel Jibra'il (AS) sometimes appeared to the Prophet (PBUH) in the form of which companion?
questions.explanation: Jibreel would at times appear in the form of the handsome companion Dihyah al-Kalbi.

questions.prompt: How many angels did Allah send to aid the believers at the Battle of Badr?
questions.explanation: Surah Al-Anfal (8:9) says Allah reinforced the believers with one thousand angels.

questions.prompt: After the Prophet (PBUH) was rejected at Ta'if, the angel of the mountains offered what?
options: To crush the people of Ta'if between the mountains
questions.explanation: The angel of the mountains offered to destroy Ta'if, but the Prophet declined, hoping their descendants would believe.

questions.prompt: According to a hadith, for whom do the angels lower their wings?
questions.explanation: A hadith says the angels lower their wings for the seeker of knowledge, pleased with what he seeks.

questions.prompt: Which of the following do angels lack, according to Islamic belief?
questions.explanation: Angels have no gender, no need for food, drink or sleep, and never disobey Allah.

questions.prompt: Who will be the first to be raised on the Day of Judgment?
questions.explanation: The Prophet (PBUH) said he will be the first to be raised on the Day of Judgment.

questions.prompt: What is 'Shafa'ah'?
options: Intercession on the Day of Judgment
questions.explanation: Shafa'ah is the intercession granted to the Prophet (PBUH) for the believers on the Day of Judgment.

questions.prompt: Which two prophets' wives are cited in the Quran as examples of disbelievers?
questions.explanation: Surah At-Tahrim cites the wives of Nuh and Lut as examples of those who disbelieved.

questions.prompt: In the traditions of Badr, the angels who aided the believers are described wearing what?
questions.explanation: Seerah traditions describe the angels at Badr wearing white turbans.

questions.prompt: What does the Arabic word 'Mala'ikah' (angels) imply?
options: Messengers of light who obey Allah
questions.explanation: Mala'ikah derives from the root meaning 'to send' — angels are Allah's messengers of light.

questions.prompt: In his true form, Jibra'il (AS) is described in hadith as having how many wings?
questions.explanation: A hadith describes Jibreel appearing in his true form with six hundred wings.

questions.prompt: What does 'Jannah' literally mean?
questions.explanation: Jannah literally means 'garden', and is the Quranic term for Paradise.

questions.prompt: Which gate of Paradise is reserved for those who fast?
questions.explanation: Ar-Rayyan is the gate of Paradise through which those who fast will enter.

questions.prompt: What is 'Yawm al-Hisab'?
options: The Day of Reckoning and Account
questions.explanation: Yawm al-Hisab is the Day when every soul is taken to account for its deeds.

questions.prompt: The command for the angels to prostrate to Adam (AS) appears first in which surah?
questions.explanation: Surah Al-Baqarah (2:34) records the command for the angels to prostrate to Adam.

questions.prompt: Which surah describes a day whose length is fifty thousand years?
questions.explanation: Surah Al-Ma'arij (70:4) refers to a day whose measure is fifty thousand years.

questions.prompt: On which night do the angels and the Spirit descend in abundance?
questions.explanation: Surah Al-Qadr says the angels and the Spirit descend on the Night of Power.

questions.prompt: What is 'Yaum ad-Din'?
questions.explanation: Yaum ad-Din, the Day of Requital, is a Quranic name for the Day of Judgment.

questions.prompt: According to the Prophet (PBUH), angels are made from light, jinn from fire, and humans from what?
questions.explanation: A hadith states angels were created from light, jinn from smokeless fire, and humans from clay.

questions.prompt: Receiving the book of deeds in the right hand signifies what?
questions.explanation: The righteous receive their record in the right hand, while the wicked receive it in the left or from behind.

questions.prompt: The 'Kursi' (Footstool) of Allah is mentioned in which verse?
questions.explanation: Ayat-ul-Kursi (2:255) mentions the Kursi of Allah encompassing the heavens and the earth.

questions.prompt: Upon whom did Allah send down the 'Sakinah' (tranquility)?
options: The believers, as mentioned in the Quran
questions.explanation: The Quran says Allah sent down Sakinah, tranquility, upon the believers, e.g. Surah Al-Fath (48:4).
